record.original_question: For an interval k-coloring of the unit interval, let c(m, k) be the minimum number of cuts needed so that the interval can be partitioned into m disjoint unions of intervals, each containing exactly 1/m of the measure of every color class. Determine whether c(m, k) = (m − 1)k for all m and k; in the source this conjecture is explicitly marked as solved by Alon.

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE: c(m, k) = (m − 1)k. ... REMARK: The conjecture has now been proved by Alon.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $k, m \ge 1$ be integers. Consider the unit interval $[0,1]$ partitioned into finitely many subintervals, each colored with one of $k$ colors (an "interval $k$-coloring"); for each color $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$, let $\mu_i$ denote the total length (Lebesgue measure) of the subintervals of color $i$. A "splitting with $c$ cuts" is a choice of $c$ points $0 \le x_1 \le \dots \le x_c \le 1$ that subdivide $[0,1]$ into $c+1$ intervals, together with an assignment of these $c+1$ intervals into $m$ groups $A_1,\dots,A_m$, such that for every color $i$ and every group $j$, the total length of color $i$ inside $A_j$ equals $\mu_i / m$. Let $c(m,k)$ denote the smallest integer $c$ such that, for every interval $k$-coloring of $[0,1]$, a splitting with $c$ cuts exists. Prove or disprove: $c(m,k) = (m-1)k$ for all positive integers $m$ and $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical necklace splitting problem. The upper bound $c(m,k) \le (m-1)k$ was proved by Noga Alon (1987) using a topological (Borsuk–Ulam type) argument, and the matching lower bound is elementary, so $c(m,k) = (m-1)k$ holds for all $m,k$. The problem is solved.

status_evidence.title: Splitting necklaces - Noga Alon
status_evidence.snippet: Alon proves that (m-1)k cuts suffice for any k-colored necklace to be fairly split among m thieves, matching the trivial lower bound.
status_evidence.claim: c(m,k) = (m-1)k is established by Alon's 1987 theorem on necklace splitting.
